productAcceptance: None. Only explicitly listed and fingerprint-bound systemd units are covered. Other launchers, accounts, unknown writers, real old DS/SDK/MR entry points, full-domain stop-write, machine reboot and production migration remain unverified. externalRestartBlocked, persistentExternalExclusion and stopWriteProvable stay false; scores remain 0/20, 1/63 and M0 11/12.
implementation: Every unit is validated by name and fragment SHA-256 before any mask or stop. Quarantine masks first, verifies the /dev/null link directly, stops and waits for inactive, and never auto-unmasks after failure.

Transient systemctl is-enabled output is not used as mask proof because it can remain 'transient'. Mask state is read from /etc/systemd/system or /run/systemd/system links; is-active=4 after unload maps to inactive.

Receipts bind fragmentPath and fragmentSha256. When a transient fragment has been deleted, release allows the missing original only if no replacement exists in trusted standard paths; a replacement is rehashed and mismatches refuse.

Release requires masked plus inactive, never starts the old unit, and reports declaredRestartBlocked/persistentDeclaredExclusion only for receipt-listed units. All global external-exclusion and stop-write flags remain false.
testRuns: Initial implementation failed mask verification because transient is-enabled did not become masked. A dedicated probe established the /dev/null link and post-stop start refusal, and mask verification was corrected to inspect that link directly.

Stopped transient units then produced is-active=4 and deleted fragment files. The adapter now handles unload state and carries fragmentPath plus digest in the quarantine receipt so release remains identity-bound without accepting replacements.

The active-release test initially assumed systemctl start would work after unmask, but a stopped transient definition no longer existed. The test now recreates the same unit before asserting MIGRATION_SYSTEMD_RELEASE_BLOCKED; this was a test correction, not a product bypass.

Final remote suite, three consecutive runs plus final: each 5 tests, 4 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip. The full test kills MainPID and observes a new PID before quarantine, then verifies start refusal and unchanged heartbeat. Logs: tmp/integration/migration-systemd-quarantine-e84/remote-final.log.
Final cleanup finds no dsh-e84 mask links. Remote and local SHA-256 match for the production module and test.

Local related combination: 106 tests, 91 pass, 0 fail, 15 skipped. check:client and all 26 documentation tests pass. Final npm test: 1915 tests, 1837 pass, 0 fail, 78 skipped (tmp/integration/migration-systemd-quarantine-e84/root-final.log).
preservedFailures: The transient is-enabled misread, is-active=4 handling gap, deleted-fragment release failure and incorrect active-test assumption are all retained as development evidence rather than hidden by the final green result.
Machine reboot was not performed. persistentDeclaredExclusion refers to the on-disk mask and declared unit identity, not a completed reboot acceptance test.
No real old DS/SDK/MR service, user profile, external non-systemd launcher or production process was touched.
limitations: W06.15 remains in_progress. Real old entry points, other launchers/accounts, full write-handle closure, machine reboot and production acceptance remain open.
The adapter operates only on explicit unit names with matching fragments. It does not discover or claim a complete launcher closure.
Systemd mask is a launcher fence, not a filesystem or storage write fence and not a substitute for draining open handles.
